name: Security Incidents
blurb:
This section tracks open incidents reported on the status pages of 12 AI infrastructure and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Lambda, Fireworks AI, Baseten, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs. It counts how many incidents each provider has open at a given time, not a curated list of disclosed security breaches, so it works as an operational health signal rather than a security news feed. Status pages are checked multiple times a day and logged daily, giving a running count back to mid-August 2026.

Because it draws on provider-published status pages, it will catch outages and provider-declared incidents, but it will miss anything a company does not post to its own status page, including disclosed vulnerabilities, data exposures, or research findings about model behavior. Read it as a proxy for provider reliability stress, not as a security-incident archive.

As of September 5, 2026, the tracker shows zero open incidents across all 12 providers, following a quieter stretch since late August. The busiest period was August 14 through 25, when 2 to 4 incidents were open concurrently most days, peaking at 4 on August 24. Lambda has been the most incident-prone provider by far, with incidents flagged on 62 of 142 checks, about 44 percent, versus 21 of 148 for OpenAI, 14 percent, and 18 of 148 for Fireworks AI, 12 percent. Cohere, Anthropic, Baseten, and Deepgram each cleared over 97 percent of checks incident-free.

reading.body:
Lambda's infrastructure has been far less reliable than peers, reporting incidents on 44 percent of operational checks since mid-August 2026, compared to 14 percent for OpenAI and 12 percent for Fireworks AI.

The data tracks incidents as they appear on provider status pages, not as formal security disclosures. This means it catches real-time outages and operational stress but misses vulnerabilities, data exposures, and model behavior issues that companies do not publish on their own dashboards. It is a reliability signal, not a security audit.

A sharp spike in concurrent incidents between August 14 and 25 peaked at four open issues on August 24, then subsided. By early September, all tracked providers showed zero open incidents. The pattern suggests either a temporary wave of infrastructure strain during that window or heightened incident reporting during that period. The data does not distinguish between the two.

Reliability differences between providers matter for AI deployment because infrastructure downtime directly interrupts compute availability. Companies building on top of these platforms face variability in uptime that correlates with their ability to scale. The data shows Lambda presents higher operational risk than the cohort average, while Cohere, Anthropic, Baseten, and Deepgram have each maintained incident-free operations over 97 percent of the observation period.
